continue through the end of the workweek as the ridge axis moves

90s Wednesday through Friday. The only difference in the latter
half of the week will be an uptick in wind velocities associated
with a storm system moving through the Northern Plains. This
system will drag the dryline east to the Big Country, which may
become a focus for storm development Thursday evening, but
probabilities of any convection overcoming the cap this far east
are slim.

"""
.KEY MESSAGES...

- Generally hot and dry conditions are expected through Monday
 with only a few isolated afternoon showers and thunderstorms.

- Cooler and wetter weather returns Tuesday and remains through
 the end of next week.

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday afternoon)

Generally hot and dry conditions are expected this weekend.
Westerly mid and upper level flow today will push a dryline into
the Permian Basin helping to push temperatures into the 90s. Hot
but not terribly so for this time of year. A mid level cap will
suppress most convection though an isolated storm or two is
possible east of the dryline, especially in the lower Trans Pecos.
Flow backs from a more southwesterly direction Sunday pulling the
dryline back farther west. An upper disturbance moving across the
region will cause storms to develop along the dryline in the Big
Bend extending north to the Pecos River.

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)

Heat and dry conditions continue into Monday before cooler and
wetter conditions return. A ridge amplifies over East Texas,
backing flow from a more southerly position, and sending a series
of disturbances over the CWA from Mexico. In addition, a trough
over the West Coast slowly moves east and further destabilizes the
atmosphere over the area. Model agreement remains poor so details
are difficult to forecast at this time though there is agreement
of good rain chances with the best chance being Wednesday and
Thursday. Lower heights and abundant clouds should keep highs in
the 80s and limit instability needed for severe thunderstorms so
the greatest severe weather threat may be localized flash
flooding. Despite good rainfall recently, the soils can likely
hold a bit more water so the greatest flood threat will be in
urban areas. Rain chances diminish late next week but do not
disappear completely.

Hennig
"""

down across much of the I-35 Corridor. With dry dewpoints moving

southwest counties where there might still be rain as well.

inversion increases back northward. Initially a shortwave ridge over
TX blocks the moisture return, but upstream troughing will be
effective in nudging the shortwave ridge eastward by Monday. Prior

deep inversion into Monday, but the latest runs show a weaker and
more shallow front that will allow for some good overrunning rains.

rain. Some of WPC's highest QPF amounts are saved for Tuesday
morning for around Austin and into much of the Coastal Prairies.

broken down the overrunning pattern and partly because western
counties will be seeing the return of a shortwave ridge. Some
residual showers are forecast for Wednesday, but we don't see that
producing much QPF, and there could be a cap that suppresses this
built up low level moisture. The warmer temperatures return Thursday
after a near normal temperature day Wednesday.

"""
.KEY MESSAGES...

- Hot and mostly dry summer weather continues this week. Practice
 heat safety and stay cool and hydrated.

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Saturday)

Mid-level ridging remains in control early this morning and is
expected to lead to continued hot and dry weather through the next
week. In the short term, afternoon highs and associated heat indices
have been right around Heat Advisory thresholds, but not widespread
enough to warrant the issuance of one. Once again, Thursday will
feature highs in the upper 90s to around 105 along the southern Rio
Grande Plains. Heat indices will hover between 103-107 with a few
spots, particularly in the Coastal Plains briefly touching 108-109
this afternoon. A weak disturbance rounding the base of the ridge
will send some low level moisture inland this afternoon, primarily
along and east of the I-35 Corridor, where we will carry 20 PoPs
this afternoon and early evening. A brief heavy downpour or two
along with an isolated thunderstorm is possible but not much beyond
that. On Saturday, hot and dry weather resumes with highs in the
mid 90s to 103 along with heat indices in the 102-108 range.

.LONG TERM...
(Saturday night through Thursday)

Sunday and beyond, the mid-level ridge slides further west and
closes off any sort of window of opportunity for showers or storms.
Highs each day Saturday through Tuesday will top out in the mid to
upper 90s to around 103. Long range guidance from the CFS does
indicate a bit of a quick switch to a more active pattern as El Nino
takes shape this Fall in the months of September and October, but we

and marginal heat index values, we'll forego issuing additional

weeks, the threat for larger grassland/wildfire activity is
expected to increase into early next week.

Dunn

(Thursday night through next Tuesday)

next week which should correspond to a slight increase in surface
temperatures during this time. While it still appears that deep
mixing will allow dewpoints to fall appreciably during peak

the western periphery of the ridge Saturday into Sunday. This will
likely result in some pooling of moisture across southeast Texas
that may eventually spread into our southeastern/eastern counties
over the weekend. If this does occur, then heat indices would
likely climb well above 105 degrees requiring additional heat
headlines.

Otherwise, the main story will continue to be the threat for
wildfire activity across the region as continued drying and

starts.

Dunn

pushing our highs in the mid 90s to near 100 degrees, with the

to gradually weaken, and likely being replaced by weak upper level
troughing from Wednesday through the end of the work week,
